name: Candace
overview: Candace was a female ruler known as the queen of Ethiopia, referenced in the New Testament book of Acts (ACT 8:27). Her title indicates she held a position of significant authority in Ethiopia during the time of the early Christian church. Beyond her royal status, Scripture does not provide further personal details about her.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Candace' appears as a proper name in Acts 8:27 without a specified meaning. Additionally, she is identified by the title 'Queen of the Ethiopians,' which directly denotes her royal position over Ethiopia. These names highlight her status and role rather than offering a deeper linguistic meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Candace beyond her identification as queen of Ethiopia. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Candace's significance in the biblical narrative lies in her role as a reigning monarch during the spread of the gospel in the early church era. Her mention in Acts 8:27 situates her within the context of the Ethiopian eunuch's encounter with Philip, which underscores the reach of the gospel beyond Israel to distant nations. As queen, she represents the openness of Gentile rulers to the message of Christ, serving as a backdrop for the conversion story recorded in Scripture.
